- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid sharp upward moves after 2–3 consecutive downward price days unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.70).
